legend: After a long day, Alice and Bob decided to play a little game. The game board consists of n$$$n$$$ cells in a straight line, numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$, where each cell contains a number ai$$$a_i$$$ between 1$$$1$$$ and n$$$n$$$. Furthermore, no two cells contain the same number.

A token is placed in one of the cells. They take alternating turns of moving the token around the board, with Alice moving first. The current player can move from cell i$$$i$$$ to cell j$$$j$$$ only if the following two conditions are satisfied:
the number in the new cell j$$$j$$$ must be strictly larger than the number in the old cell i$$$i$$$ (i.e. aj>ai$$$a_j  \gt  a_i$$$), and
the distance that the token travels during this turn must be a multiple of the number in the old cell (i.e. |i−j|modai=0$$$|i-j|\bmod a_i = 0$$$).

Whoever is unable to make a move, loses. For each possible starting position, determine who wins if they both play optimally. It can be shown that the game is always finite, i.e. there always is a winning strategy for one of the players.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the number of numbers.

The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤n$$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$). Furthermore, there are no pair of indices i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$ such that ai=aj$$$a_i = a_j$$$.
output: Print s$$$s$$$ — a string of n$$$n$$$ characters, where the i$$$i$$$-th character represents the outcome of the game if the token is initially placed in the cell i$$$i$$$. If Alice wins, then si$$$s_i$$$ has to be equal to "A"; otherwise, si$$$s_i$$$ has to be equal to "B".
note: In the first sample, if Bob puts the token on the number (not position):
1$$$1$$$: Alice can move to any number. She can win by picking 7$$$7$$$, from which Bob has no move.

2$$$2$$$: Alice can move to 3$$$3$$$ and 5$$$5$$$. Upon moving to 5$$$5$$$, Bob can win by moving to 8$$$8$$$. If she chooses 3$$$3$$$ instead, she wins, as Bob has only a move to 4$$$4$$$, from which Alice can move to 8$$$8$$$.
3$$$3$$$: Alice can only move to 4$$$4$$$, after which Bob wins by moving to 8$$$8$$$.
7$$$7$$$, 8$$$8$$$: Alice has no move, and hence she loses immediately.

legend.ai: 经过漫长的一天后，Alice 和 Bob 决定玩一个小游戏。游戏棋盘由一排 n$$$n$$$ 个格子组成，格子编号从 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$，每个格子中都包含一个介于 1$$$1$$$ 和 n$$$n$$$ 之间的数字 ai$$$a_i$$$。此外，没有两个格子包含相同的数字。
棋子被放置在其中一个格子中。他们轮流在棋盘上移动棋子，Alice 先手。当前玩家只有在满足以下两个条件时，才能将棋子从格子 i$$$i$$$ 移动到格子 j$$$j$$$：
新格子 j$$$j$$$ 中的数字必须严格大于旧格子 i$$$i$$$ 中的数字(即 aj>ai$$$a_j  \gt  a_i$$$)，并且
本回合棋子移动的距离必须是旧格子中数字的倍数(即 |i−j|modai=0$$$|i-j|\bmod a_i = 0$$$)。
无法进行移动的玩家输掉游戏。对于每个可能的起始位置，确定在双方都采取最优策略时谁会获胜。可以证明游戏总是有限的，即其中一名玩家始终存在必胜策略。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤105$$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$)，表示数字的数量。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤n$$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$)。此外，不存在满足 ai=aj$$$a_i = a_j$$$ 的下标对 i≠j$$$i \neq j$$$。

output.ai: 输出 s$$$s$$$ —— 一个由 n$$$n$$$ 个字符组成的字符串，其中第 i$$$i$$$ 个字符表示棋子初始放置在单元格 i$$$i$$$ 时的游戏结果。如果 Alice 获胜，则 si$$$s_i$$$ 必须等于 "A"；否则，si$$$s_i$$$ 必须等于 "B"。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，如果 Bob 将棋子放在数字上（而不是位置上）：
1$$$1$$$：Alice 可以移动到任意数字。她可以选择 7$$$7$$$，从而获胜，因为 Bob 无法移动。
2$$$2$$$：Alice 可以移动到 3$$$3$$$ 和 5$$$5$$$。移动到 5$$$5$$$ 后，Bob 可以移动到 8$$$8$$$ 并获胜。如果她选择 3$$$3$$$，则她会获胜，因为 Bob 只能移动到 4$$$4$$$，之后 Alice 可以移动到 8$$$8$$$。
3$$$3$$$：Alice 只能移动到 4$$$4$$$，之后 Bob 可以移动到 8$$$8$$$ 并获胜。
7$$$7$$$、8$$$8$$$：Alice 无法移动，因此立即输掉比赛。
